events.title: The C Programming Language book published
events.summary: Kernighan and Ritchie's book became the de facto C language definition for over a decade.
events.about: The book taught C as the language of Unix systems programming — writing shells, utilities, drivers, and portable tools. Sample programs in the book (hello world, parsers, small utilities) became how a generation learned to code close to the metal.

narrative.whyChosen: Before ANSI C, this book was the specification developers actually used worldwide.
narrative.whyImportant: It codified K&R C and spread Unix systems programming practices beyond Bell Labs.
narrative.problemSolved: C lacked a formal standard; teams needed a stable, readable reference to write portable code.
